To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• A neural network trained to predict the minimal solution length can be used to estimate the heuristic cost of a given state in the Rubik’s cube domain.

1) the neural network can predict the minimal number of moves with high accuracy; 2) the network can be used as a heuristic for solving Rubik's cube; 3) the network-based heuristic is competitive with the state-of-the-art heuristics; 4) the network-based heuristics might be the best option for some use-case scenarios.

• we propose a new approach to heuristic learning for the Rubik’s Cube domain, • we use machine learning for the heuristic learning task, • we train a neural network for predicting a number of moves required for solving a given instance of the Rubik’s cube, • we use the trained network in an informed forward-search planner, • the experimental results show that our heuristic is competitive with the state-of-the-art.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can deep neural networks learn to solve combinatorial problems in the Rubik’s cube domain?
the question: “Can a deep learning approach help to design a powerful heuristic function for a combinatorial problem?”.

the question whether a heuristic function can be learned in a domain where a human-designed heuristic function exists, and if so, whether the learned heuristic function is better than the human-designed one.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the learning approach can compete with the state-of-the-art, however, it is not always the best option and it is still not as good as a hand-crafted heuristic.
learning-based heuristic is a promising direction for solving the Rubik’s cube problem.
the learning approach has the potential to be the best choice for the Rubik’s cube domain and should be further investigated on other domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully trained a deep neural network to predict the number of moves required in a Rubik’s cube puzzle.
deep learning can be used to construct powerful and easily-computed heuristic functions.
deep learning is a promising approach to construct heuristics in the planning domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
machine learning techniques can be used for solving combinatorial search problems.
deep learning approaches might be a promising alternative for designing heuristics for planning problems in the future.
deep neural networks can be successfully applied to the Rubik’s cube problem.
